Datavault Shares Crash as Bitcoin Treasury Remains Trapped on Biconomy Amid 4-Month Withdrawal Delay

Casa co-founder Jameson Lopp highlighted that Bitcoin treasury company Datavault (DVLT) saw its stock price crash, tumbling 49.55% over a 24-hour period. The plunge follows the company’s notice to investors disclosing that its entire treasury reserves are held on crypto exchange Biconomy, but despite submitting transfer and withdrawal requests for four months, it has been unable to withdraw any BTC from the platform. — link

South Korea’s Second-Largest Crypto Exchange Bithumb Confirms Security Breach

According to Yonhap News Agency, South Korea’s second-largest cryptocurrency exchange, Bithumb, confirmed that an unauthorized external party accessed its internal mobile groupware system, resulting in a personal data leak. The exchange discovered the incident on October 27 and is investigating whether customer information was compromised.

Two other South Korean financial institutions, Mirae Asset Global Investments and Daishin Securities, were also confirmed to have suffered cyber intrusions. Daishin Securities disclosed that the personal and credit information of 38,490 customers had been leaked. South Korea’s Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) is investigating the incidents. — link

US Treasury Secretary: Crypto Leadership Strengthens Dollar Dominance, Stablecoins Expand Treasury Demand

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated at Ripple’s Swell conference that global reserve currency dominance is shifting from a military umbrella to a "technology umbrella," positioning US leadership in digital assets as a critical tool to reinforce the dollar’s global standing; noting that over 90% of stablecoins are dollar-backed and heavily collateralized by US Treasuries.

Bessent highlighted that stablecoin expansion in emerging markets directly drives demand for government debt and serves as an important funding source for the Treasury; addressing Congress’s failure to pass the Clarity Act, Bessent pledged to leverage Treasury’s convening power alongside the SEC and CFTC to advance administrative rulemaking and establish regulatory guardrails to prevent the recurrence of crypto debanking. — link

Third-Party Analytics Vendor Amplitude Suffers Security Incident, Leaking Contact Info for a Small Subset of Coinbase Users

SlowMist CISO 23pds posted that a data leak involving Coinbase has been confirmed, though it remains unconfirmed whether passwords or funds were compromised. The hacker obtained contact information for more than 70,000 users. Subsequently, Coinbase Support clarified that Coinbase itself did not experience a data breach. The incident originated from a security breach at third-party data analytics vendor Amplitude, which affected several of its clients, including Coinbase, leading to the leak of contact details for a small subset of Coinbase users. Coinbase stated that it found no evidence of unauthorized access to its internal systems, that customer funds remain entirely unaffected, and that it is notifying affected users and relevant regulatory authorities in accordance with legal requirements. — link

Brazil’s Largest Private Bank Itaú Unibanco Becomes Country’s First to Notify Regulator of Crypto Brokerage Operations Under New Rules

Brazil’s largest private bank, Itaú Unibanco, notified the central bank of its cryptocurrency trading and custody operations on October 27, becoming the country’s first bank to do so under the new digital-asset rules. The framework allows banks already authorized by the central bank to offer crypto services through a notification process, while dedicated virtual-asset service providers must apply for operating authorization. The deadline for existing operators to submit notifications or applications is October 30. Itaú has offered crypto services since December 2023 and currently supports 15 cryptoassets. — link

Bank of Canada Raises Policy Rate by 25 Basis Points to 2.5% in First Hike in Three Years

The Bank of Canada on October 28, 2026, raised its target for the overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, the first increase since July 2023. The Bank Rate is now 2.75% and the deposit rate is 2.45%. The move aims to reduce the risk that persistently high energy prices spread to the prices of other goods and services. Governing Council said the policy rate may need to rise further, but it will proceed carefully given the uncertainties. — link

Bloomberg: Over $170M in Unusual Hyperliquid Oil Perp Orders Raise Spoofing Suspicions

According to Bloomberg, market surveillance firm Solidus Labs identified over $170 million in unusual orders placed through two Hyperliquid accounts between March 8 and 10, amid sharp oil price swings linked to the Iran war. The activity raised concerns about potential spoofing in oil perpetual futures markets.

The trader repeatedly placed and canceled large orders on one side of the order book while executing trades on the other, with a cancellation-to-execution value ratio of roughly 30:1, generating about $119,000 in profits over three days. The activity primarily involved Brent crude perps. Solidus said the pattern resembled spoofing but acknowledged that manipulative intent remains unproven. Hyperliquid Labs emphasized that all orders, cancellations and trades are recorded on a transparent public blockchain and can be independently reviewed. — link

Fed Holds Rates Steady at 3.75%–4.00% in 10–2 Vote, Two Officials Favor Hike

The Federal Reserve voted 10–2 on October 28 to maintain the federal funds rate target range at 3.75%–4.00%. The FOMC said economic activity continues to expand at a strong pace, supported by resilient domestic spending, strong productivity growth, and robust capital investment, despite elevated geopolitical uncertainty. Job growth has kept pace with labor force growth, while unemployment has changed little. Inflation remains elevated, and the Committee will assess incoming data to determine the appropriate policy stance to return inflation to its 2% target. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented, favoring a 25-basis-point rate hike.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank will vote on interest rates at seven of its eight scheduled policy meetings in 2027, reducing that number to six in 2028. The remaining meetings will focus on broader monetary policy discussions. — link

🚨 TODAY: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at 3.75%–4.00%, citing strong economic activity and still-elevated inflation.
